Empirical Research Plan  
“Do disappointing wage outcomes reduce police performance? Evidence from New Jersey final-offer arbitration, 1978-1996”

---------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
---------------------------------------------------------
Strategy: Difference-in-differences (DiD) with an event-study (dynamic DiD).

Rationale  
• The FOA decision date cleanly splits “before” and “after” periods for each bargaining unit.  
• Treatment (union loses FOA) versus control (union wins FOA) is plausibly quasi-random: once a case reaches arbitration, arbitrators must pick one of two final offers and anecdotal evidence indicates decisions are close calls.  
• We observe multiple years of outcomes on the same police departments, allowing department and year fixed effects to net out time-invariant heterogeneity and statewide shocks.  
• Event-study coefficients reveal whether pre-trends are parallel and how long any treatment effect persists.

Because assignment is nearly random, a simple post-minus-pre comparison would already be credible; DiD/event study increases precision and allows rich diagnostics.

---------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
---------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
Treated = 1 if, in a given FOA case, the arbitrator chose the management’s (lower-wage) offer – i.e., the union “lost” the arbitration.

Control group  
Departments whose unions “won” and received their full wage demand form the control group.

Treatment timing / event date  
Year 0 = fiscal year in which the FOA award is announced and becomes effective.  
We code an event-time variable τ ∈ {-3,…,+3}. Outcomes for τ<0 are pre-treatment; τ≥0 are post-treatment. (We drop departments that had another arbitration within the ±3 window.)

---------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
---------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel trends – Absent treatment, winners and losers would have followed the same performance path.  
Plausibility: Arbitrator choice is nearly random; event-study will test for pre-trend equality.

A2. No simultaneous shocks differentially correlated with the award (excludability).  
Plausibility: Negotiations are idiosyncratic to the municipality; we will control for crime incidence and municipality-year covariates.

A3. Stable Unit Treatment Value (no spillovers).  
Plausibility: Each police department is a separate labor market; an unfavorable award in Town A is unlikely to affect effort in Town B.

A4. No selective attrition linked to treatment (e.g., officers quitting).  
Plausibility: Police turnover is low, but we will examine staffing counts to verify no treatment-induced exit.

A5. Treatment is as-good-as-random conditional on reaching arbitration.  
Plausibility: Supported by institutional accounts; we will show balance on pre-award covariates.

---------------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation
---------------------------------------------------------
T1. Selection into arbitration winners/losers not random (e.g., stronger unions might systematically win).  
Mitigation:  
• Demonstrate balance on pre-award outcomes and covariates.  
• Include arbitrator fixed effects where available.  
• Instrument “loser” with an indicator for arbitrators historically favoring management (first-stage F>10).

T2. Differential crime shocks (crime wave hits losers).  
Mitigation:  
• Control for contemporaneous crime incidence (number of reported crimes by type).  
• County*year fixed effects to absorb regional shocks.

T3. Measurement error in UCR clearance rates (misreporting may itself respond to morale).  
Mitigation:  
• Use two performance measures: (i) clearance rate, (ii) arrests per officer. Consistent effects across both lessen concern.  
• Restrict to Part I Index crimes, less susceptible to discretionary downgrading.

---------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
---------------------------------------------------------
```r
# --------- Packages ----------
library(data.table)      # fast data
library(fixest)          # FE regressions & event study
library(did)             # Callaway-Sant’Anna
library(multiwayvcov)     # cluster-robust vcov
# -----------------------------

# --------- 1. Load & merge ----------
arb <- fread("arbitration_nj_1978_1996.csv")   # dept_id, award_year, union_win, mgmt_win
ucr <- fread("ucr_police_departments.csv")     # dept_id, year, crimes_reported, crimes_cleared, arrests_total, sworn_officers

# keep only final-offer cases
arb <- arb[foa_case==1]

# merge
setkey(arb, dept_id)
setkey(ucr, dept_id)
data <- merge(ucr, arb, allow.cartesian=TRUE) # many years per case

# --------- 2. Construct variables ----------
data[, clearance_rate := crimes_cleared / crimes_reported]
data[, loser := as.integer(mgmt_win==1)]             # 1 = treated
data[, winner := as.integer(union_win==1)]
data[, event_time := year - award_year]              # τ
data <- data[event_time >= -3 & event_time <= 3]     # balanced window
data[, post := (event_time >= 0)]

# --------- 3. Main DiD ----------
did_main <- feols(clearance_rate ~ loser*post | dept_id + year,
                  data = data, cluster = ~dept_id)
summary(did_main)

# --------- 4. Event study ----------
data[, tau := factor(event_time)]
est <- feols(clearance_rate ~ i(event_time, loser, ref = -1) | dept_id + year,
             data = data, cluster = ~dept_id)
iplot(est, ref.line = 0, xlab="Years since award", ylab="Clearance rate diff")

# --------- 5. Robustness: alternative outcome arrests per officer ----------
data[, arrests_rate := arrests_total / sworn_officers]
rb <- feols(arrests_rate ~ loser*post | dept_id + year,
            data = data, cluster = ~dept_id)
summary(rb)
```
Additional robustness not shown: re-weight by department size, placebo leads, wild-cluster bootstrap, arbitrator IV.

---------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
---------------------------------------------------------
Theory (reference-dependent preferences) predicts a decline in effort when actual pay falls short of the salient reference point (the union’s demand).  
Direction: Clearance rates and arrests should fall in loser departments relative to winners.  
Magnitude (back-of-the-envelope): A 2–3 percentage-point drop in clearance (baseline ≈ 25% for Part I crimes) and a 5–8% drop in arrests per officer.

---------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DiD)
---------------------------------------------------------
C1: Parallel pre-treatment trends  …………… 1  
C2: No anticipation / timing sharp ………… 1  
C3: No differential contemporaneous shocks … 0.5  
C4: Stable composition / no selective attrition 0.5  
C5: SUTVA – no spillovers …………………… 1  
Total (out of 5) ……………………………… 4.0

Overall, the design is strong but hinges on verifying parallel trends and ruling out crime-shock confounds.
